history.description: Adds a guarantee underneath the sync rather than another fix on top of it: a value this device has changed but not yet got onto the server can no longer be replaced by anything coming back from it, full stop. Deciding that by timestamp was never sound — a phone whose clock runs fast stamps the future, a version too old to know about the timestamps strips them and makes its own stale values look freshly written, and a write that slips through unstamped has no time at all. Each of those ends with your edit quietly replaced by an older one. The app now remembers what it last actually sent, so it can tell a value the server has from one it has never seen, and no clock is consulted for that.
highlights: 🛡️ چیزی که ثبت کردی و هنوز به سرور نرسیده، دیگه تحت هیچ شرایطی با نسخه‌ی قدیمی‌تر جایگزین نمی‌شه

history.description: Fixes water, calories and anything else logged shortly after opening the app reverting to an older value once the app was closed and reopened. Recording that something changed was gated on the account session having finished loading, which takes a few hundred milliseconds after every start. Anything logged in that window was neither marked as changed nor queued to send, so nothing downstream knew it had happened, and the next time the app checked the server it replaced the value with the older one held there. Whether a server is reachable has no bearing on whether something changed on the device, so it no longer waits for it — the send itself already handled being unable to run yet.
highlights: 💧 ثبت آب و کالری بلافاصله بعد از باز کردن اپ دیگه با بستن و باز کردن برنمی‌گرده

history.description: Two devices used in the same stretch no longer overwrite each other. Until now the whole account was stored and replaced as a single record, so whichever device saved last won outright and everything the other had changed since was thrown away. Each value now carries the moment it last changed, and the two versions are combined value by value, newest of each winning — change your weight on one phone and log a meal on the other and both survive. A value that was deleted stays deleted rather than being restored by the other device. Deliberately built so a phone still running the previous version reads the new records exactly as before: the values sit where they always did and the timestamps ride alongside under a name older versions never look at, because those versions delete any value they don't find, and a nested layout would have made one erase itself.
highlights: 🔀 تغییرات هم‌زمان روی دو گوشی دیگه همدیگه رو پاک نمی‌کنن — هر مقدار جداگانه ادغام می‌شه

history.description: Fixes two ways an edit could fail to reach a second device. An edit made in a popup that closes without navigating — height, gender, birth date, a weigh-in, a logged meal — waited a second before being sent, and backgrounding an installed PWA freezes its JavaScript, so on a phone that timer often never fired and the edit stayed on the device. Edits are now sent the moment the app goes away, and a device marks itself as having unsent changes the instant one is made rather than only after a send fails, so anything caught mid-flight is retried at the next launch. Separately, whether to accept the server's copy was decided by comparing timestamps that each device wrote from its own clock: a phone running even a few minutes fast would stamp the record into the future and then refuse every later update for good. That decision now rests on whether this device has anything unsent, and on whether the content actually differs.
highlights: 🔄 تغییرات پروفایل، وزن و وعده‌ها دیگه موقع بستن برنامه از دست نمی‌رن
⏱️ اختلاف ساعت بین دو گوشی دیگه جلوی همگام‌سازی رو نمی‌گیره

history.description: First public release. The beta-v3 line becomes the app everyone gets, and the version number resets to 1.0.0 to mark it — note this is a lower number than the 2.0.1 it replaces, which is fine: nothing in the app orders versions, it only asks whether the running one differs from the deployed one. Every piece of account data is stored on the server and follows the account between devices; the only things that stay on a device are the ones that describe the device rather than the account — which account is signed in here, whether this browser has dismissed the install hint, and which changelog it has already shown. A device picks changes up whenever the app returns to the foreground, not only at a cold start — but never while it still has edits of its own the server hasn't accepted, since taking an older snapshot then would lose a write outright.

history.description: The profile page gained a date-of-birth field below weight and height, picked as a Gregorian date on three wheels. history.description: Reworked the headline above every chart on the progress pages. history.description: Burned calories from a workout are no longer written to the day's activity total the instant an exercise is ticked off. Ticking now only marks the exercise; the estimate accumulates untracked and is presented once, when the workout is completed, under the exercise/set summary in the confirmation popup — with a toggle deciding whether it counts toward the day, and a note that the figure is an estimate from the standard MET formula, the logged bodyweight and an assumed per-set duration rather than a measurement. The estimate is now derived from the checklist on demand instead of being accumulated tick by tick, so unchecking an exercise no longer has to reverse a previously written number out, and committing it sets the day's total rather than adding to it, so completing the same workout twice cannot double it.

history.description: Reworked how a meal is inspected and corrected on the daily log. The "+" on a meal card now asks how you want to log the food — manually or with the AI — instead of jumping straight into the manual search, which is what made the AI route effectively invisible from this screen. Tapping anywhere else on the card expands it in place rather than opening a summary popup, and the foods logged for that meal are now listed under the protein/carb/fat/fiber totals they add up to. Tapping any of them opens an editor for its amount, which rescales that entry's calories and macros. Editing works off the amount recorded when the food was added and never off the previous edit's result, so adjusting a portion back and forth returns the exact original numbers instead of drifting a gram at a time.

history.description: Swapped in the new background image. Encoded at WebP quality 95 with smart chroma subsampling rather than the ~6KB a lower quality would produce: the image is one large smooth gradient, and the failure mode of over-compressing a gradient is banding — flat plateaus with a visible step between them, worst across the dark lower two thirds on an OLED panel. Measured every candidate encoding against the source pixel by pixel; at q95 the whole frame stays within 5/255 even after the browser upscales it to cover the viewport, so it is 25KB instead of 6KB. That is a one-time fetch since the file is precached, which is the right side of the trade.

✨ با کیفیت بالا فشرده شده تا گرادیان پله‌پله و پیکسلی نشه، مخصوصاً توی قسمت‌های تیره

history.description: The app-wide background is now the reference image itself rather than a CSS gradient approximating it. The source PNG was 1.1MB, which is far too heavy for something that paints under every screen — re-encoded as WebP it is 9.1KB, a 99% reduction, because a smooth gradient is exactly the kind of image WebP compresses almost to nothing while a PNG stores it pixel by pixel. Also added webp to the service worker's precache patterns, which only covered png/svg/ico before: without it the background would have been the one asset missing from the offline cache, fetched over the network on every cold start.

history.description: Fixed account deletion, which was deleting neither the account nor all of its data. It never removed the auth user at all — only signed out — so the username stayed registered forever and could not be used to create a new account. Deleting one now goes through a new delete-account edge function, which is the only place that can do it: removing an auth user requires the service-role key, which must never reach the browser. The function identifies the account from the caller's own token, deletes its data row and then the user itself, and the username is free again. On the data side, three keys survived a delete and came back at the next login: the archived per-day calorie history and the daily calorie target (resetDailyLog only cleared today's meals — this is the leftover calories that were visible after recreating an account), the learned-foods cache (never cleared by anything), and the profile fields, which were cleared only after the emptied snapshot had already been pushed, so the server kept its copy. Underneath all of them, the reset now also sweeps every key the sync layer declares as synced, so a key added later can't quietly survive a reset by being forgotten. Deletion also reports failure instead of pretending: if the server can't be reached the account is left exactly as it was and the reason is shown, rather than wiping the device and leaving the real account behind. The error screen's recovery button is unchanged — it still wipes the data and keeps the account.

history.description: Turned the calories and activity charts into bar charts. Both are daily totals — an amount belonging to one particular day rather than a value passing through it — so a column per day says what they are, where a line implied a smooth journey between days that never happened. The day, week and month ranges draw one bar per day at that day's own figure, with no averaging anywhere; only the 6-month and year ranges aggregate, one bar per month holding that month's daily average, which is the point of those ranges. The headline number follows the same rule instead of always reading میانگین: the per-day ranges now show مجموع, the sum of the bars on screen, and only the two monthly ranges show an average. Bars need a zero baseline, so those two charts get their own axis that always starts at zero and picks a step fine enough to keep the grid readable — a centred axis would have cut the columns off at the bottom and made a 1900-vs-2000 day look twice as tall. The weight chart is untouched: it's a measurement, not a total, so it keeps its line, its gaps and its average.

history.description: Redrew the weight chart as a hand-written SVG instead of chart.js, following Apple Health's visual rules. The Y axis now picks its own step from the spread of the readings in view — under 5kg apart gets 1kg lines, 5 to 10kg gets 2kg, and anything wider gets 5kg — so a week where the weight barely moved is no longer a flat line squashed against the middle of an oversized scale. A far-away goal escalates the step further rather than stacking a dozen gridlines. A day with no weigh-in stays genuinely missing: it gets no dot, and the line runs straight from the last real reading to the next one rather than dipping toward zero, and a range holding a single reading draws that one hollow ring with no line at all. Styling follows Apple: neon purple at 2.5px, hollow rings for the readings, solid faint horizontal gridlines against dashed vertical ones, and the numbers on the right edge. The other charts (calories, activity) still use chart.js — only the weight page swaps in the new component.

history.description: Added a calorie-goal calculator to the daily-calories page. A new block sits directly under the chart: before a target exists it's a single 'محاسبه هدف کالری من' button, and afterwards it shows the number with its goal type and a pencil to edit. The popup collects gender, age, height, weight, activity level and goal, pre-filled from whatever the profile already knows so most people only pick the last two, and previews the resulting number live as the choices change. The logic lives in a new src/utils/calorieEngine.ts: Mifflin-St Jeor BMR, TDEE via the activity multiplier (1.2 / 1.375 / 1.55 / 1.725) and the goal adjustment (-500 / 0 / +300), each exported as a pure function with the persistence kept separate. That engine deliberately does not write emad-daily-calorie-target itself — it hands the result to dailyLogEngine, which already owns that key, so the key keeps exactly one owner and the chart's dashed target line picks the new number up with no extra wiring. The profile inputs likewise go back to the engines that own them, so filling this form in also records today's weight and fills the height the BMI card needs. Age, activity level and goal are new synced keys and are cleared by a factory reset. The manual target stepper stays as an override.

📉 فرمول استاندارد Mifflin-St Jeor برای سوخت‌وساز پایه، ضریب سطح فعالیت برای نیاز روزانه، و کسر/اضافه‌ی هدف

history.description: Enabled the month/6-month/year ranges on the activity chart — they showed a 'coming soon' note before — and applied the range fixes to the calories chart properly. Both are daily totals rather than point-in-time measurements, so they now say so: a day with nothing logged counts as zero instead of a hole, which keeps their lines continuous, and a monthly figure divides by the days of that month that have actually elapsed instead of only the days that happened to get logged (a month with three logged days no longer reports itself as if every day had looked like those three). The headline average follows the same rule, so it can no longer disagree with the line drawn right under it. Weight is unchanged: a skipped weigh-in is genuinely missing data, not a zero, so it keeps its gaps and averages only real measurements. A month with nothing logged at all still shows no point rather than a zero, so months from before you started using the app don't draw a flat line.

history.description: Reworked the stat charts' axes. The Y-axis used to stretch to a distant target line while keeping the data's own step, so a 101kg current weight with an 85kg goal drew ~19 gridlines 1kg apart — the step is now re-picked as the range grows and that case lands on 85/90/95/100/105. Fixed a real pre-existing bug in the same file while verifying it: snapping the centred axis minimum to a step multiple could push the data high enough to fail the top-headroom test at every step, so the loop escalated without ever converging — an ordinary 98-101kg trend produced a -200..400 axis. The minimum now slides back up (never past the data's own minimum, so containment holds) instead of escalating. The date under the average now describes the selected period itself rather than the first/last day that happens to have an entry: the week tab reads as a 7-day window, month as 30 days, and 6-month/year from the first of their oldest month. The 6-month range stopped plotting raw entries and now shows exactly six ticks — the last six month numbers — each the average of what was logged that month, matching the year range; it therefore joins month/year as an aggregated view, so water and activity show their existing 'coming soon' note there until their own bucketing is designed.

history.description: Checking an exercise off during today's workout now estimates and logs the calories it burned, using the standard MET formula (Calories = MET × 3.5 × weightKg / 200 × durationMinutes) against your latest logged weight — added to today's total right alongside manually-logged activity, and reversed automatically if you uncheck it. Every exercise now carries its own metValue (approximate, per the Compendium of Physical Activities' general categories). The formula itself lives in a pure domain function (domain/services/calorieCalculator.ts) with zero UI-layer math, matching this project's existing plain-function engine pattern rather than introducing a new state-management dependency.

history.description: Fixed the water page not updating right after logging from the quick-add shortcut while already on that page. It navigates there after logging, but React Router doesn't remount on a navigate() to the same URL — it just pushes a new history entry — so the page's initial-read state never re-ran and kept showing the pre-log count until you left and came back. It now re-reads the count and goal on every navigation to the page (keyed off the router's per-navigation history key, which changes even for a same-path navigate), so the update shows immediately.

history.description: Fixed the water glass showing almost no fill at low counts (1-2 out of 8) and only a thin sliver at 3 out of 8, despite the count and full-glass state both being correct. It was drawing the water as a full-height rectangle clipped to the glass's tapered outline via clip-path: url(#...) — WebKit doesn't reliably repaint that kind of clip-path reference as the clipped rectangle's height keeps changing every animation frame, so it stayed clipped to a stale, near-empty shape at every fill level except the two extremes it happened to render correctly at rest. Replaced it with a directly-computed trapezoid path (both jug shapes: the big glass on the water detail page, and the smaller tile on the progress page) that needs no clip-path at all, so there's nothing left to go stale.

history.description: Reworked the slide-to-complete button's drag visual: instead of a detached circle handle sliding along the track over a separate blurred trail, the pill itself now stretches — at rest it's a 68px circle, and dragging elongates it into a capsule whose right end follows the finger, with the arrow riding centered on the capsule's round leading edge. history.description: Swept the whole codebase for anything still painting a solid green or yellow surface after the 2.1.52 glass conversion, and converted the rest. The program builder's day cards lost their vivid forest-to-lime gradient (the largest solid surface left in the app) and became glass panels; the .day-card-gradient class was deleted rather than left as dead CSS. The meal cards' round add button was the last solid coloured button fill (lime with a black icon) and is now .glass-action with a white icon. The yellow tint circles behind icons in the update prompt, workout header, side-menu avatar and the AI 'تخمینی' badge became glass chips — the icons keep their accent colour, the surfaces don't. The account popup's logout button swapped a hardcoded forest outline for the shared .ghost-action, and the wheel picker's selection band swapped dark forest lines for white ones now that it sits inside a glass modal. Verified by scanning every main screen at runtime: the only element still painting a solid theme colour is the app's own page background, which is the intended base canvas. Yellow now exists solely as a text/icon accent (active nav tab, AI sparkle, warnings); the only remaining coloured fill anywhere is the toggle switch's on-state, which needs colour to signal on/off at all.

history.description: Finished the glass conversion across the whole app. Every popup still using the old solid-green card (account, height, what's-new, update-available, install hint, workout header/complete, free-meal settings, error screen) now uses the same glass panel as the newer ones, so nothing reads as left over from the previous design. Removed every solid yellow button fill — the primary call-to-action is now a new .glass-action (a lighter fill and brighter rim than .glass-chip, so it still carries CTA weight without a colour outside the system) with white text instead of black, and the picked option in a choice group is .glass-selected (brighter still, plus a full ring, since selected/unselected can no longer lean on yellow-vs-green). .selector-pill became glass as well, and the remaining solid-green surfaces inside popups (steppers, number/unit inputs, changelog rows) became glass chips. The toggle switch's on-state moved from yellow to the palette's lime — with every button fill now glass it would have been the last yellow fill in the app, and lime is already the app's affirmative colour while still contrasting against the white thumb. Yellow survives only as an accent (active nav tab, icon tints), never as a button fill. 'پاک کردن حساب کاربری' is now red, since it's the one irreversible action in that popup and read like neutral secondary text next to logout.

history.description: Fixed the intermittent popup/drawer backdrop blur on iOS for good — the maddening 'sometimes blurred at the agreed strength, sometimes not at all'. Root cause: every popup and the quick-add backdrop rendered inside SideMenu's motion.div, and whether framer-motion leaves a transform on that wrapper at any given moment is timing-dependent; on WebKit a transformed ancestor changes what backdrop-filter may sample, so the blur worked or silently didn't depending on which state the wrapper happened to be in. Two structural fixes: (1) ModalOverlay now renders through a portal to document.body — no transformed ancestor, ever — plus an explicit -webkit-backdrop-filter and a mount ramp (insert at blur(0), switch to blur(25px) two frames later) since WebKit also fails to paint a backdrop-filter already present at DOM insertion; the ramp doubles as a fade-in. (2) The quick-add drawer stopped using backdrop-filter entirely: Layout now puts a real CSS filter blur(15px) on <main> while the drawer is open — a plain filter on the content itself always renders, no sampling dependency to break. Verified: drawer open/close toggles the main filter, modal backdrop is portaled to body at computed blur(25px), tap-outside-to-close and all four quick-add shortcuts unchanged.
highlights: 🌫️ بلر پشت پاپ‌آپ‌ها و کشوی افزودن دیگه شانسی نیست — همیشه و با همون شدت توافق‌شده رندر می‌شه
📖 محتوای پشت کشوی افزودن حالا واقعاً محو می‌شه و نوشته‌ها توی هم نمی‌رن

history.description: The quick-add circle no longer reads as a disc floating over the bottom navigation — it's now part of the bar's actual shape. The cause was structural: the bar and the circle were two overlapping .glass-panel elements, and each drew its own hairline rim, so the bar's rim ran straight through the circle while the circle's rim closed underneath it. Both are now a single SVG silhouette — a pill unioned with a semicircle centred on its top edge — carrying one continuous fill, one continuous hairline (matching .glass-panel's own values) and a drop-shadow that follows the whole outline, so there are no interior seams left to give it away. The button keeps only the icon and its hit area, with the plus nudged into the bump's exposed half. The path is measured in real pixels via ResizeObserver so the bump stays a true circle at any width. Quick-add drawer behaviour is unchanged (all four shortcuts and tap-outside-to-close re-verified).

history.description: The slide-to-complete button's handle now exactly fills the track's height (68px, no inset gap) instead of sitting slightly smaller with a small border around it. history.description: Restyled the slide-to-complete button to match the bottom navigation bar: same pill shape and glass treatment, with the three yellow chevrons replaced by a single round glass handle holding an arrow, sized and styled like the nav's own round button. Dragging now pulls a 30px blurred trail across the track instead of a yellow fill — it fades in over the first 28px so there's no blurred patch sitting under the handle at rest. The trail deliberately carries no mask-image: WebKit can drop backdrop-filter entirely when combined with a mask (this app has already hit iOS backdrop-filter bugs), so the leading edge is capped by the handle circle instead, and the same GPU-layer promotion ModalOverlay relies on is applied so the blur paints reliably on iOS. Verified drag, release-below-threshold snap-back, and full-drag completion all still work.

history.description: Water and activity became square tiles too, so the progress page is now a clean 2x2 grid of equally-sized tiles. Built the water feature out properly: the tile draws a glass that literally fills to today's share of the goal, and the water page dropped its chart entirely (a glass count is a small number you top up through the day — 'how full am I now' is the useful view, not a trend line) in favour of a big jug that fills as you log, plus a tappable grid of glasses: tap the glass you're up to and it fills to there, tap the one you're already at to take it back, with +/- buttons for going past the goal. Added a settable daily glass goal (default 8, range 4-16) since a fillable glass grid needs a target to fill toward; it syncs across devices like every other setting. Activity's tile deliberately has no progress ring — unlike calories there's no activity goal, and a ring at some arbitrary fraction would be inventing one. Also fixed a real pre-existing bug: factory reset never cleared the water or activity logs (both were missing from resetApplication). Removed the now-unused StatCard component.

history.description: Performance: eliminated the app's single biggest constant GPU load — the background glow (MeshGradientBackground, present under every screen including login and the error page) was two huge divs with filter: blur(110px) running infinite framer-motion x/y/scale/opacity loops (12s/15s, forever). On iOS WebKit a 110px blur keeps two multi-megapixel intermediate buffers alive and the never-ending animation re-composited them at 60fps, permanently pegging the phone's GPU — hot device even at idle, and seconds of tap latency because every real interaction had to fight the background for GPU time (this, not just the 2.1.43 viewport loop, was the remaining cause of the reported browser hang/heat). Replaced with static radial gradients — a radial gradient IS a soft glow: painted once, no filter, no animation, visually near-identical (verified by screenshot comparison), zero ongoing cost. This was the only infinite animation in the app (verified by grep). Benefits both browser and installed PWA — cooler device and better battery everywhere.

history.description: Critical fix: opening the app in an iPhone BROWSER tab (Safari/Chrome, not the installed PWA) could peg the CPU — frozen UI, phone heating up. Root cause was a side effect of 2.1.39's viewport-height fix: documentElement.clientHeight was included in the height measurement in every mode, but in an iOS browser tab the layout viewport is routinely taller than the visible area while the URL bar is showing (the classic 100vh quirk). Sizing the app off it made the document scrollable, scrolling collapsed/expanded the toolbar, that fired the (also newly-added) visualViewport resize listener, the measured height flipped between the two values, and the whole app re-laid-out every frame — a genuine feedback loop. The installed PWA was unaffected (no toolbar, all candidates equal), which is why it only showed in the browser. Browser tabs now measure exactly as they did before 2.1.39 (window.innerHeight only); the extra clientHeight/screen.height candidates apply only in iOS standalone mode where the webview always covers the whole screen and they're guaranteed correct. Verified all three prior scenarios still pass (standalone stale clamps to 844, browser tab tracks 800, settled standalone unchanged).

history.description: Fixed the stat detail pages' chart rendering at a stale, too-narrow width in the installed PWA — pushed against the right edge (RTL start-alignment of a canvas narrower than its wrapper) and clipped at the screen edge. Same root cause as the 2.1.39 viewport bug: iOS standalone cold launch lays the page out against a stale viewport and WebKit's late correction doesn't reliably reach chart.js's own ResizeObserver, freezing the canvas at the stale size. StatChartPage now mirrors MobileContainer's exact settle-signal set (staggered timers, resize, orientationchange, pageshow, visualViewport resize) and imperatively calls chart.resize() on each — a no-op when the size is already right. The chart wrapper also gained overflow-hidden so a transiently mis-sized canvas clips inside the panel instead of painting past the screen edge. Verified: baseline canvas exactly spans its wrapper; a forced stale-narrow canvas (270px vs 350px) snaps back to full width on the first settle signal.

history.description: Fixed the installed (home-screen) PWA intermittently not filling the full screen — a dead black strip would sometimes appear under the app, because window.innerHeight reports a stale, too-short value on cold launch and after the keyboard closes, and WebKit doesn't reliably fire any event when it later corrects itself. The JS-measured height now (1) also listens to visualViewport resize (keyboard dismissal often only announces itself there, not on window.resize) with an extra late settle timer, and (2) in iOS standalone mode (navigator.standalone, which covers home-screen installs from both Safari and Chrome since both are WebKit) clamps up to screen.height in portrait — a standalone app with viewport-fit=cover always covers the entire screen, so screen.height is correct even while innerHeight is still stale, without waiting on WebKit to catch up. Regular browser-tab behavior is unchanged (verified: container tracks innerHeight exactly there). Verified via simulated standalone (stale innerHeight 800 vs screen 844 → container renders 844).

history.description: Added a daily calorie target, mirroring the weight page's target feature exactly: a settable goal (TargetCaloriesModal, 100-calorie steps), a dashed target reference line on the calories chart, a target/current-calories row block, and the goal now shown on the progress overview's calorie card the same way the weight card already does. history.description: Grew the stat detail pages' chart panel further (46% to 58% of the screen). Fixed the Y-axis so a distant target-weight line no longer drags the whole chart's resolution down around it — the axis is now sized from the real data alone (keeping fluctuation visible) and only extended afterward, in fixed steps, just far enough to fit the target in too. Added a hard rule that the highest data point can never sit above two-thirds of the chart height, so the latest/current value always has visible headroom above it instead of pinning to the ceiling. Simplified the day/week/month/6-month x-axis labels to just the day number (dropping the repeated month name on every tick) and the year view's month labels to just the month's 1-12 number instead of its full name.

history.description: Removed the old zoomable weight chart from the weight-entry page (/settings/weight) — the weight chart now only lives on the progress detail page. Fixed the progress overview's weight card goal label to say 'وزن هدف: ...' instead of just the bare number. Rebuilt the stat detail pages' Y-axis to always center the data within exactly 4 gridlines instead of floor/ceil-ing outward (which pushed a narrow value range toward the bottom edge), added x-axis offset so a single point renders centered instead of pinned to the plot edge, and gave week/month fixed-width calendar-day buckets (real gaps for days with nothing logged, instead of the chart shrinking to only the days with data) while year now aggregates into 12 monthly-average points. The weight chart also gained a dashed target-weight reference line (the Y-axis now stretches to include the target too, so the gap to goal is visible at a glance), and its panel grew from ~33% to ~46% of the screen since the header/range-selector/average text left almost no room for the chart itself at the old size. Removed the glass-panel press-scale animation's stray hairline along the very top edge of the flush-to-top panel (it's pinned to the screen edge, so a border there read as an unwanted seam) and gave pages built around that panel (all 4 progress detail pages) a way to bleed their background under the safe-area/status-bar strip instead of showing a plain gap above them in the installed PWA.

history.description: Removed the accidental press-scale animation on the progress detail pages' top glass panel and the weight page's target/current-weight box — tapping a nested button (back, +, range pill, target-weight row) was also visibly scaling the whole outer container due to CSS :active bubbling to ancestors. Replaced the progress page's weight card (which embedded its own mini chart, target/current-weight rows, and add-weight button) with a plain stat card matching the calorie/water/activity cards exactly — tap it to open the weight detail page instead. Fixed a real filtering bug in the new stat detail pages' day/week/month/6-month/year range selector: the day range was actually filtering the last 7 days, week was showing 30 days, and month was showing 90 days (each one off by a slot) — day now correctly shows just today, week the last 7 days, and month the last 30.

history.description: Added a real detail page for each of the progress page's four stats (weight, daily calories, water, activity), styled after an iOS Health-app chart: a glass panel flush to the top of the screen (~1/3 of it), a day/week/month/6-month/year range selector, an average value with its date range, and a line chart whose Y-axis never shows more than 3 gridlines or a step finer than the stat's own minimum (1kg for weight). Water and activity had no tracking at all before this — both now have their own history store and a quick-add affordance (water logs a glass in one tap; activity opens a small calorie stepper). Daily calories previously discarded the whole day's log the moment the date rolled over — its final total is now archived into a real history instead, so it can be charted too.

history.description: Added a third, last-resort fallback to AI meal logging: when a food matches neither the local/learned database nor the external API, Gemini's own nutrition estimate (now requested directly in the parse-meal prompt, alongside name/quantity/unit) is used instead of leaving the item unmatched — clearly labeled 'تخمینی' (estimated) in the results list so it's never confused with a real database value, and still saved to the learned-foods store for next time.

history.description: Fixed the AI meal-parsing edge function's CORS allowlist to also accept dev.gampetoo.com (it was only allowing the production domain and localhost:5173, so requests from the dev domain were silently rejected by the browser). Grew the Iranian food database from 28 to 66 items (missing staples like زیره پلو and drinks/fruit/vegetables like نوشابه, سیب, خیار). The AI matching path now falls back to a live external lookup (the same Open Food Facts API the manual search already uses) when a food isn't in the local database, and permanently saves whatever it finds into the account's own learned-foods list (synced across devices) so future lookups — AI or manual — never repeat the network round-trip. A food that still isn't found anywhere is skipped with a warning instead of blocking the rest of the meal from being logged. Also fixed serving-unit matching ('قاشق' now matches 'قاشق غذاخوری' instead of silently falling back to the wrong default unit).
highlights: 🌐 رفع باگ CORS که باعث می‌شد «افزودن با هوش مصنوعی» روی dev.gampetoo.com کار نکنه

🌍 وقتی غذایی توی دیتابیس نیست، خودکار آنلاین پیدا و برای همیشه به دیتابیس شخصی‌ات اضافه می‌شه
⚠️ اگه یکی از غذاها هیچ‌جا پیدا نشه، فقط همون رد می‌شه، نه کل وعده

history.description: Fixed the AI meal-parsing edge function, which was failing end-to-end: switched from gemini-1.5-flash (doesn't exist for the configured API key) to gemini-flash-lite-latest, the one model that both exists and has working free-tier quota for that key. Verified with a real request through the deployed function. Also committed the Supabase CLI's project scaffolding (config.toml, .gitignore) so the setup is reproducible.

history.description: Implemented the real logic behind 'افزودن با هوش مصنوعی': the free-text meal description is now sent to a Supabase Edge Function (supabase/functions/parse-meal) that proxies to the Gemini API server-side, keeping the API key off the client bundle entirely (the client never talks to Gemini directly, and the key is never a VITE_* env var). The extracted (name, quantity, unit) items are matched against the app's real local food database (aiFoodMatching.ts, reusing foodSearch.ts's caloriesForServing) and shown as a confirmable itemized list with per-item calories and a total before anything is actually logged; unmatched items are called out separately instead of being silently dropped. Requires the user to deploy the edge function and set the GEMINI_API_KEY secret in their Supabase project — instructions provided separately, since this sandbox has no live Supabase project to deploy to or test the round-trip against.
highlights: 🤖 «افزودن با هوش مصنوعی» حالا واقعاً کار می‌کنه — توضیح متنی‌ات رو با Gemini تحلیل می‌کنه و قبل از ثبت، خلاصه‌ی کالری رو نشونت می‌ده

history.description: Disabled swiping between pages — every bottom-nav tab is its own React Router route, and WKWebView's native edge-swipe-to-navigate-history gesture lives on the same right edge as SideMenu's own open-drawer gesture in this RTL app, so dragging from the edge could pop back to the previous route (visible as two pages caught mid-transition) instead of, or as well as, opening the menu. Added overscroll-behavior-x: none to html, the standard fix for this in Safari/WebKit — SideMenu's own drag-to-open isn't affected since it runs on pointer events it captures directly, not this browser-level gesture. Verified no regression: the side menu still opens via the same edge-drag.

history.description: Disabled pinch-zoom and double-tap-zoom app-wide. Two layers, since some browsers ignore the viewport meta's user-scalable=no for accessibility reasons: index.html's viewport meta gained maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=no, and html got touch-action: manipulation in index.css (the more reliable modern approach) — manipulation still permits panning/scrolling, so it doesn't affect the app's scrollable containers or the wheel-pickers' own touch-action: pan-y. Verified no scroll regression on the main page and the wheel-picker.

Also: switching modes now warns first if there's anything logged today (window.confirm, same pattern as logout/delete-account) since a per-meal breakdown and a single daily total can't be reconciled into one view — confirming clears today's log (dailyLogEngine's new hasTodaysLoggedEntries/resetDailyLog), canceling leaves the mode and data untouched. No warning when there's nothing to lose.

history.description: Added a selectable calorie-tracking mode: per-meal (existing 9-slot cards) or daily (one unified list, no meal categorization). Both modes write into the exact same dailyLogEngine storage, just under different slot keys — nothing is migrated or deleted when switching, so it's non-destructive by construction. The Progress page's daily-calorie total now sums every logged entry regardless of which mode wrote it (new getTodaysTotalCalories in dailyLogEngine.ts), so it stays correct across a mode switch. A new row in the side menu (SideMenu.tsx) opens a picker to change the mode any time; if it hasn't been chosen yet, the ثبت روزانه page's وعده غذایی tab shows an inline choice prompt first. Verified end to end: logged 381 calories in daily mode, confirmed it appears on the Progress page, switched to per-meal mode via the side menu, confirmed the 9 meal cards render empty (data preserved under its own key, not lost) while the Progress total still correctly shows 381.

history.description: Fixed every popup in the app (all of them share ModalOverlay) rendering with no blur behind them on a real iOS device — a screenshot showed the height picker's card sitting directly on top of fully sharp, unblurred page content. Verified the CSS/positioning itself was correct (Chromium renders it fine, backdrop-filter computes to blur(25px) and covers the full viewport) — this is a well-known WebKit bug where backdrop-filter on a position:fixed element intermittently fails to render at all. Forced the blurred backdrop onto its own GPU compositing layer (transform:translateZ(0) + will-change:backdrop-filter), the standard mitigation for this exact bug.

history.description: The 2.1.18 fix (height:100% cascade) made the standalone-PWA gap worse: it removed the only mechanism (a native dvh recalculation, incidentally triggered whenever the user scrolled) that let the layout self-correct, so the too-short initial height became permanent instead of fixable by scrolling. Replaced it with a JS-measured height: MobileContainer now sizes itself from window.innerHeight in a small hook that re-measures a few times shortly after mount (plus on resize/orientationchange/pageshow), since iOS reports a stale too-short value on a standalone cold launch that only settles after a later layout pass. This reproduces what scrolling used to accidentally trigger, automatically, without the user having to scroll.
highlights: 🐛 رفع (این‌بار درست) مشکل فاصله‌ی خالی زیر صفحه در حالت نصب‌شده روی آیفون — بدون نیاز به اسکرول کردن

history.description: Fixed a black gap below the home indicator (and the bottom nav floating above it, not flush with the screen edge) when the app is opened as an installed home-screen PWA on iOS. Root cause: MobileContainer sized itself with height:100dvh, and WebKit has a long-standing bug where dvh under-reports the true viewport height in standalone display mode. Switched to a height:100% cascade (html/body/#root all explicit height:100%, MobileContainer using h-full instead of h-dvh), which resolves against the WKWebView's actual content bounds instead of the buggy viewport-unit calculation.
highlights: 🐛 رفع باگ فاصله‌ی خالی زیر صفحه و ناهم‌راستایی منوی پایین وقتی اپ از روی صفحه‌ی اصلی گوشی (نصب‌شده) باز می‌شه

The add-food popup's food list is now capped to about 4 rows with its own scrollbar and a visible scroll-position indicator next to it.

Also fixed a real bug found while building this: a popup nested inside a pressable glass-panel card could stop responding to taps after the page scrolled, because CSS :active bubbles up and can turn that ancestor card into a containing block for the popup's fixed positioning — popups now always render as siblings of any card that opens them, and the side menu's own blur filter (which had the same footgun even at zero blur) is now only applied while the drawer is actually animating.

history.description: Major release merging seven weeks of beta work into main (previously at 1.3.0). history.description: Added a configurable weekly free-meal count. A new "وعده آزاد" button on the nutrition-plan page opens a stepper to set how many free meals you get per week (defaults to 1, same as before). The free-meal card on the daily nutrition page now tracks and shows remaining/total for the current 7-day cycle, confirms with the right wording whether you just used one of several or your only one for the week, and says the week's free meals are used up once they hit zero. The cycle resets to exactly the configured count every 7 days — unused meals never carry over into the next week.
highlights: 🍕 تعداد وعده آزاد هفتگی حالا قابل تنظیمه

history.description: Changed the weight-tracker chart's date labels from the Jalali (Shamsi) calendar to Gregorian, matching every other date shown in the app except the home page's greeting, which keeps its Gregorian-with-Jalali-in-parentheses format on purpose.
highlights: 📅 تاریخ نمودار وزن به میلادی تغییر کرد

history.description: Restyled the slide-to-complete handle: dropped the black circular knob in favor of three bare yellow chevrons (bigger than the old single icon), fading from full color on the left to faint on the right to read as a directional swipe hint. The yellow fill is now fully hidden at rest, fades in only once dragging starts, and its leading edge softens into the track instead of cutting off sharply.
highlights: 👉 طراحی جدید دستگیره دکمه اسلایدی (بدون کادر مشکی، فلش‌های زرد محوشونده)

history.description: Replaced the tappable "تمرین امروز رو انجام دادم" / "پیاده روی امروز رو انجام دادم" buttons with a slide-to-complete gesture (framer-motion drag), so finishing a workout or walk needs a deliberate swipe instead of a single tap. Dragging past 75% of the track snaps forward to a completed checkmark state and confirms; releasing earlier snaps back to the start. The "رفتن به کتابخانه تمرین‌ها" button (a plain navigation link, not a completion action) is unchanged.
highlights: 👉 دکمه اتمام تمرین حالا اسلایدی است (بکشید تا تایید شود)

history.description: Fixed the checkbox tap-drop still happening on the workout-library exercise/warmup screens: the previous fix only stopped each row from shrinking on tap, but the group card wrapping the rows still scaled down on any tap inside it (including on a checkbox), shifting the row out from under the finger — same class of bug the sets/reps steppers could hit too. Cancelled the press-scale on those outer group cards as well, matching the nutrition menu exactly.
highlights: 🏋️ رفع مشکل سخت بودن تیک زدن چک‌باکس‌ها در کتابخانه تمرین‌ها

history.description: Restyled the workout library and exercise-detail screens to match the nutrition menu: fixed missing horizontal padding (cards ran edge-to-edge), and replaced the ✅/⬜ emoji-in-a-button toggle for exercises and warmup groups with real checkbox inputs, matching the nutrition menu's touch/tick behavior exactly.
highlights: 🏋️ هماهنگ‌سازی طراحی و تیک‌خوردن کتابخانه تمرین‌ها با برنامه غذایی

history.description: Removed the "set a password" prompt entirely — every account now signs up with a password from the start, so the feature (and the flaky check it used) no longer applies to anyone. Restricted the 🤦 forgot-to-log button to the workout page only (it was leaking onto the nutrition page too, since both share the same header component). Reworked the day-shift itself to no longer move the program's startDate — it now only nudges an internal cycle counter, so the displayed start date stays exactly as originally set.
highlights: 🧹 حذف کامل درخواست تنظیم رمز عبور و اصلاح دکمه فراموشی ثبت تمرین

history.description: The new 🤦 workout-page button now performs the real "forgot to log yesterday's workout" action instead of a placeholder: it shifts the program cycle one day forward (today shows what was supposed to be tomorrow's workout), replacing the old plain text link that used to live in Settings for this. Verified the program's startDate correctly moves back a day when confirmed.
highlights: 🤦 دکمه فراموشی ثبت تمرین حالا واقعاً چرخه برنامه رو یک روز جلو می‌بره

history.description: Added an icon-only "forgot to log" button (🤦) to the top-left of the workout page header. Tapping it opens a popup explaining what it does, with a "فراموشی ثبت تمرین" button that retroactively marks today's workout as completed (for when you did it but forgot to tap "انجام دادم" in time) and a "متوجه شدم" button that just closes the popup with no effect.
highlights: 🤦 اضافه شدن دکمه فراموشی ثبت تمرین به صفحه تمرین

history.description: Added a "مکمل و ویتامین‌ها" (supplements & vitamins) section to both the workout-day and rest-day meal plans, right after "قبل خواب" — with a dedicated bank of the most commonly used sports supplements (creatine, whey protein, multivitamin, omega-3, vitamin D3, magnesium, BCAA, caffeine/pre-workout, glutamine, vitamin C, zinc, ZMA, beta-alanine, collagen), kept separate from the regular food search so it never gets suggested as a meal food. Also fixed the nutrition menu pages having no horizontal padding (buttons/cards ran edge-to-edge) — now matches the width used on Settings and other pages.
highlights: 💊 اضافه شدن منوی مکمل و ویتامین‌ها با بانک مکمل‌های ورزشی پرکاربرد

history.description: Fixed the "set a password" prompt wrongly reappearing after an app update for accounts that already had one. It used to decide based on whether a live Supabase session existed right now, which can drop out for reasons unrelated to the account actually having a password (e.g. a token-refresh hiccup right around an update reload). It now checks a persisted local flag set the moment the account first successfully authenticates, decoupled from live session state.
highlights: 🐛 رفع نمایش نادرست دوباره پیام «رمز عبور تنظیم کن» بعد از آپدیت

history.description: Added a dedicated gym-foods bank to the food catalog (boiled/grilled chicken breast, turkey breast, canned tuna, egg whites, lean ground beef, whey protein, low-fat cottage cheese, brown rice, sweet potato, quinoa, rice cakes) covering the staples researched as most common in workout meal plans. Each meal (breakfast, post-workout, snack, etc.) now surfaces its typically-relevant foods at the top of the browsable list instead of a fixed catalog order. Also rebalanced the food-list font weights: the food's name is now bold and the calorie amount normal weight, instead of the reverse.
highlights: 🍗 اضافه شدن بانک غذاهای باشگاهی و پیشنهاد غذا بر اساس نوع وعده

history.description: App-wide: disabled text selection and iOS's tap-and-hold copy/lookup callout on every text and button (inputs still allow normal text selection/editing), so the app feels native instead of like a selectable document. Also audited every non-white text color against its actual background and brightened the low-contrast ones (secondary captions, error text, calorie labels) that were tuned for the old near-black theme and had fallen below readable contrast on the new green background.
highlights: 🔒 غیرفعال شدن انتخاب متن با تاچ و بهبود خوانایی رنگ‌های متن در کل برنامه

history.description: Fixed a math bug in the weight picker where the row below center rendered as the largest instead of the selected (center) row, due to a missing padding offset in the distance-from-center calculation. Also disabled the settings card's press-scale animation on this screen (it fought with dragging the wheel), locked the wheel to vertical-only scrolling (touch-action: pan-y, no horizontal drag), and switched scroll-snap from mandatory to proximity with a corrective snap-back so a fast flick can now coast through many values at once instead of resisting between every single one.
highlights: 🐛 رفع سایز اشتباه ردیف انتخاب‌شده و بهبود اسکرول سریع در انتخابگر وزن

history.description: Restyled the weight wheel picker: removed its dark green background entirely (fully transparent now), narrowed it to 3 visible rows (one above, the selected row, one below), colored the selected number and the decimal point dark green with the neighboring rows paler, removed the "کیلوگرم" label, and changed the default value to the last logged weight overall (50.00 if none exists yet) instead of always today's.
highlights: 🎨 بازطراحی انتخابگر وزن: بدون بک‌گراند، ۳ ردیف، رنگ سبز تیره

history.description: Replaced the plain number input on the weight-tracking screen with an iOS-style wheel picker: a kg column and a grams column, each scrolling and snapping to center natively, with a 3D-cylinder-style fade/scale falloff away from the selected row.
highlights: 🎡 اضافه شدن انتخابگر چرخشی (Wheel Picker) برای ثبت وزن

history.description: Added a "خروج از حساب کاربری" (log out) button next to the reset button in Settings — signs out and returns to the first screen without touching any local data, so logging back in with the same username brings everything back. Renamed "شروع دوباره" to "پاک کردن حساب کاربری" with a clearer description that it fully deletes the program and data.
highlights: 🚪 اضافه شدن دکمه خروج از حساب کاربری بدون پاک شدن اطلاعات

history.description: Split the first-run account screen into an explicit choice between "ورود" (login: username + password only, checked against the existing account) and "ثبت نام" (signup: name + username + password + confirm password), replacing the single combined form that silently signed up or logged in behind the scenes.
highlights: 👤 جداسازی صفحه ورود و ثبت نام در اولین اجرای برنامه

history.description: Fixed weight-log (and other synced) data appearing to get wiped after applying an in-app update: the PWA update flow reloaded the page to activate the new version without flushing a pending debounced sync push first, unlike every other reload path in the app. An edit made in the second before tapping "بروزرسانی" could fail to reach the server, and in a race, a stale in-flight push from the old page could even overwrite fresher local data right as the new page loaded.
highlights: 🐛 رفع گم شدن اطلاعات (مثل سابقه وزن) هنگام بروزرسانی برنامه

history.description: 1.2.5's plain on-screen stacking brought the black box back on real iOS Safari — confirming the video's hardware compositor layer really does float above normal DOM stacking there, not just bypass opacity. Reverted to the 1.2.4 off-screen approach: no black box, but the mascot is a static frame on iOS instead of animating, which is the preferred trade-off over a black box.
highlights: 🎨 رفع مجدد مشکل مربع مشکی لوگو در سافاری موبایل

history.description: The black box was gone after 1.2.4, but the mascot froze on a single frame on real iOS Safari — moving the source video far off-screen to hide it also made iOS suspend its playback entirely (a known battery-saving behavior for off-screen video). Reverted to keeping the video plainly on-screen and in normal document flow, relying on ordinary DOM stacking (the canvas simply paints over it afterward) instead of any CSS hiding trick, so it stays visible enough to keep decoding while never actually being shown.
highlights: 🎨 رفع مشکل ثابت ماندن انیمیشن لوگو در سافاری موبایل

history.description: The mascot animation still showed a black box on real iOS Safari after the 1.2.3 canvas fix, because iOS can promote an autoplaying <video> to a hardware compositor layer that ignores CSS opacity — so the hidden source video kept painting its raw black frame over the processed canvas. Moved the source video fully off-screen (position: fixed, far outside the viewport) instead of hiding it in place, and added a defensive fallback in case a device can't read video pixels back onto canvas at all.
highlights: 🎨 رفع مشکل مربع مشکی لوگو در سافاری موبایل

history.description: New mesh-gradient + noise background across the app shell (setup, error screen, main layout), and the setup-page mascot icon replaced with a looping brand animation. Fixed the animation rendering as a solid black box on Safari/iOS by replacing the CSS blend-mode approach (silently ignored on <video> in WebKit) with a canvas-based luma key.
highlights: 🎨 آپدیت بک گراند و لوگو

history.description: Cross-device account sync verified end-to-end and deployed: username + password now backs up and restores program, session, and preferences across devices, with existing local-only accounts prompted to set a password without losing any data. Fixed a race that could drop a write made right before the app reloaded, and added Cloudflare Pages deployment config (SPA routing, cache headers) alongside the existing Vercel setup.
highlights: ✨ رفع ایرادهای ظاهری و بهبود تجربه کاربری
👤 اضافه شدن قابلیت انتخاب و نمایش نام کاربری و پسوورد

history.description: Cross-device account sync via Supabase: username + PIN login now backs up program, session, workout/warmup overrides, and free-meal state to the server, so the same account picks up right where it left off on any device. Existing local-only accounts upload automatically on first login with a PIN. Offline use keeps working — changes queue locally and sync once back online.
highlights: ☁️ همگام‌سازی اطلاعات با سرور از طریق نام کاربری و رمز
📱 دسترسی به برنامه از هر دستگاهی با یک حساب

history.description: Verified and hardened the PWA update system for installed home-screen apps: added a cache-control header for version.json (Vercel's edge could otherwise serve a stale deployed-version number) and a pageshow listener alongside visibilitychange/focus so iOS Safari's back-forward-cache restores reliably trigger an update check too.
highlights: ✨ رفع ایرادهای ظاهری و بهبود تجربه کاربری
👤 اضافه شدن قابلیت انتخاب و نمایش نام کاربری (Username)

history.description: UI polish (safe-area insets for the installed app, first-run install hint popup, combined setup form, Jalali date picker) and multi-user accounts: username-based login with automatic migration for existing name-scoped users, account switching in Settings, and a production PWA update system with an in-app changelog.
highlights: ✨ رفع ایرادهای ظاهری و بهبود تجربه کاربری
👤 اضافه شدن قابلیت انتخاب و نمایش نام کاربری (Username)

history.description: First public release, rebranded as Gampetoo. Workout library (Push/Pull/Legs/Upper/Lower/Full Body) with per-exercise selection, general and per-workout specialized warm-up blocks, full nutrition plan editor (workout/rest day meal plans, food catalog, free-meal weekly lock), PWA support (installable, offline-capable, app icons), and hardened local-storage persistence.
